findings.description: The EC2 instance's user_data embeds long-lived AWS access key and secret access key values (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) directly in the Terraform configuration. These are exposed in instance user data (readable via the metadata service), cloud-init logs, and Terraform state, allowing anyone with read access to obtain working credentials.
The security group allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote administration to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-based attacks against the instance.

The security group allows HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no upstream filtering. Combined with the public subnet, public IP, and internet gateway route, the web service is fully reachable from untrusted networks.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so the attached disk is stored unencrypted at rest.
The EBS snapshot does not specify encryption, so the backup of the instance disk is stored unencrypted (the source volume is itself unencrypted).
The S3 bucket used for VPC flow log storage has no server-side encryption configuration, so captured network traffic metadata is stored unencrypted.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true makes every instance launched into this subnet automatically receive a public IP and be directly internet-routable.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true makes every instance launched into this subnet automatically receive a public IP and be directly internet-routable.
A 0.0.0.0/0 default route is associated with the route table attached to both subnets, giving instances in those subnets direct internet reachability via the internet gateway.
The VPC flow log writes to an S3 bucket that has no bucket policy, encryption, or access restrictions, so flow log data may be readable or writable beyond its intended scope.
force_destroy = true permits the bucket and all flow-log objects to be deleted non-interactively, undermining log retention and tamper-resistance of security telemetry.
